extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and Patent Registration Office staff in Malaysia
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards for filing, prosecuting, examining, amending and maintaining patent applications and patents in Malaysia under the Patents Regulations 1986 (as amended). Covers content/formatting requirements, examination procedures, timelines, fees and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees (Schedule I)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees to be paid in respect of all matters arising under the Act and these Regulations shall be as specified in Schedule I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees must be paid to the Patent Registration Office by such means and manner as the Registrar may direct; Schedule I lists fees for filing, examinations, annual fees, reinstatement surcharges, electronic vs manual rates and other items (with itemised RM amounts and associated forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms (Schedule II)
rubrics_metrics.description: The forms referred to in these Regulations are those set out in Schedule II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific requests, declarations and procedural acts must be made on the prescribed form (e.g., Form 1 for request for grant of patent, Form 5 for substantive examination, Form 20 for address for service). Schedule II notes forms menu (forms not reproduced in document).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents (Regulation 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for the grant of a patent shall contain a request for the grant of a patent; a description; a claim or claims; a drawing or drawings, where required; and an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application shall be filed at the Patent Registration Office. All five elements are mandatory where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of international applications (Regulation 5A)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall be filed in three copies; where filed in less than three copies the Patent Registration Office shall prepare the additional copies and charge prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide three copies or pay for the Office to prepare extras; applies when entering national phase or filing international applications domestically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name and declaration of inventor (Regulation 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall contain the name and address of the inventor; an inventor may submit a signed written declaration indicating he does not wish to be named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventor identity is required but a written, signed opt-out is permitted and must be submitted to the Registrar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for grant of patent and title of invention (Regulation 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for the grant of a patent shall be made to the Registrar on Form 1 together with payment of the prescribed fee; the title shall indicate clearly and concisely the subject-matter to which the invention relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form 1 and pay fees; titles must be short, clear and descriptive of the subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names and addresses format (Regulation 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names and addresses given in the application shall in all cases be the full names and addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations or incomplete addresses are not acceptable; must be full details for applicants/agents/inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and residence indication (Regulation 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant's nationality shall be indicated by the name of the State of which he is a national (or the State under whose laws a non-natural person is constituted); the applicant's residence shall be indicated by the name of the State of which he is a resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must specify State names for nationality and residence, or the constituting State for entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's right to patent (Regulation 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant is the inventor the request shall state that fact; where the applicant is not the inventor the request shall be accompanied by a statement justifying the applicant's right to the patent (Form 22 together with Form 1 and Form 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who are not inventors must supply documentary justification of entitlement using the prescribed forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common representative where multiple applicants (Regulation 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is submitted by more than one applicant and they have not appointed a patent agent to represent all of them, the request shall designate one applicant as common representative; if not designated, the first-named applicant is considered the common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common representative handles communications with the Office; designation is recommended to avoid default first-named representative status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description structure and content (Regulation 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall state the title and shall (a) specify the technical field, (b) indicate background art useful for understanding/searching/examination and cite documents where possible, (c) disclose the invention sufficiently clear and complete for a person skilled in the art to carry it out and state advantageous effects, (d) briefly describe figures in drawings, (e) describe the best mode contemplated for carrying out the invention using examples where appropriate, and (f) indicate explicitly industrial applicability and how it can be made and used where not obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description should follow the order specified unless a different order suits the nature of the invention; description must not contain drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — clarity, support and reasonableness (Regulation 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be clear and concise and fully supported by the description; the number of claims shall be reasonable considering the nature of the invention; claims should be consecutively numbered; claims must not contain drawings and should not, unless necessary, rely on references to the description or drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must define the invention in terms of technical features; where drawings exist, reference signs may be used sparingly and consistently; claims should include, when appropriate, statements identifying features necessary but part of prior art and a characterising portion (e.g., 'characterised in that').

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims (Regulation 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim (one including all features of another claim) shall, if possible at the beginning, reference the other claim(s) and then state the additional features; dependent claims are construed as including all limitations of the claims to which they refer; dependent claims referring back to a single or several previous claims should be grouped together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple dependent claims are to be interpreted as including limitations of the particular claim in relation to which they are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings requirements (Regulation 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are required only when necessary for understanding the invention; applicants may include drawings on filing if nature of the invention admits illustration by drawings; flow sheets and diagrams are considered drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the most illustrative drawing(s) with the abstract when appropriate; drawings must be executed as per physical requirements (see Reg 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content and length (Regulation 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract shall commence with a title and contain a summary of the disclosure as contained in the description, claims and drawings and, where applicable, the chemical formula that best characterises the invention; it shall indicate the technical field, allow clear understanding of the technical problem, gist of solution and principal uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should be concise, preferably not more than 150 words, must not contain statements about merits or speculative applications; each main technical feature illustrated by a drawing should be followed by its reference sign in parentheses; abstract not to contain drawings but be accompanied by most illustrative drawing(s); it must be an efficient searching instrument to decide whether to consult full specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units, terminology and consistency (Regulation 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Units of weights and measures shall be metric; temperatures in Celsius; densities in metric units; international practice observed for electrical/math/scientific units; chemical formulae use standard symbols and atomic weights; only generally accepted technical terms, signs and symbols in the field should be used; terminology and signs shall be consistent throughout application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard international units and accepted field terminology; ensure internal consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical presentation requirements (Regulation 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents should be filed in duplicate unless otherwise provided; documents must admit direct reproduction by photography/electrostatic/photo-offset/microfilming; sheets free from cracks/creases/folds and only one side used; documents on A4 paper (29.7 x 21 cm) durable, white, smooth; minimum margins 2 cm; sheets numbered at top centre in consecutive Arabic numerals; text typed/printed in dark indelible colour at least 1½ line spacing (certain formulae/graphics may be handwritten/drawn); every fifth line of description and claims shall be numbered in Arabic numerals placed to left of lines; drawings executed in durable black lines without colouring; application filed in national language or English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar may accept other sizes or require more copies; strict formatting required for reproduction and examination; deviation only as permitted by Registrar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (Regulation 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of section 26, same patent application may include: (a) in addition to independent claim for product, an independent claim for process specially adapted for manufacture and independent claim for use of product; (b) in addition to independent claim for process, an independent claim for apparatus designed to carry out process; (c) combinations thereof; subject to section 26, application may contain two or more independent claims of same category not readily covered by a single generic claim; may contain reasonable number of dependent claims even if dependent features might be inventions by themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines permissible claim groupings and acceptable number of independent and dependent claims based on unity; subject to statutory section 26 limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of application timing (Regulation 19A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where division is pursuant to objection in an Examiner's report for non-compliance with section 26, request for division must be made within three months from date of mailing of report; otherwise applicant may voluntarily request division not later than three months from mailing of Examiner's first report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict three-month time limits apply for divisional requests depending on context of examiner objection or voluntary division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures to be disregarded for prior art (Regulation 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant shall state in the request or at any time any disclosure which he is aware of which in his opinion should be disregarded for prior art purposes under section 14(3) and shall state the facts in an accompanying statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must proactively identify possible disclosures to be disregarded and provide supporting facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration claiming priority content and timing (Regulation 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration claiming priority shall state the date of each earlier application, subject to subregulation the number of each earlier application, symbol of IPC if allocated, name of State where earlier application filed or states for regional/international application, office where regional/international application was filed; if number not known it shall be furnished within three months; if IPC symbol not allocated at time state that fact; information for multiple priorities may be included in a single declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority declarations must be timely and provide specified particulars; three-month cure period for unknown numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy and translation of earlier application (Regulation 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where section 27(2) applies, applicant shall furnish certified copy of each earlier application within three months from Registrar's request; may reference another application if copy already furnished; if earlier application in language other than national/English, Registrar may require translation within three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-month compliance period; certified copies and translations are required upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections in priority declaration (Regulation 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Registrar finds requirements of regs 21 and 22 not complied with he shall request corrections/particulars/documents within three months; if applicant does not comply, Registrar shall inform applicant that declaration is deemed invalid under section 27(4) and state reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar provides a three-month cure; failure results in deeming priority invalid with reasons provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of application (Regulation 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may withdraw his application by a declaration on Form 2 addressed to the Registrar and signed by applicant or authorized agent; in case of several applicants declaration must be signed by all applicants or by agent authorized; agent-signed declarations must be accompanied by letter authorizing agent to sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal withdrawal requires Form 2 and authorization documentation where signed by agent or multiple applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date and certificate of filing (Regulation 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Registrar records the filing date he shall send to the applicant a certificate of filing in form of a copy of the request with filing date and application number marked; required correction under section 28(2) must be filed within three months of Registrar's request; Registrar shall inform applicant in writing with reasons if application treated invalid under section 28(3); drawings required under section 28(4) shall be furnished within three months of Registrar's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar issues filing certificate; three-month cure periods for corrections and drawings; applicant is informed of invalidity with reasons if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering the national phase for international applications (Regulation 25A)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application entering the national phase under sections 78O/78OA shall be subject to prescribed fees paid using Patents Form No. 2A; an applicant shall be deemed to have fulfilled the requirement of section 78O(1)(a) or 78OA(1)(a) if the international application in English has been made available by the International Bureau to the Patent Registration Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National phase entry requires prescribed fees and reliance on availability of English-language international application at IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination formal requirements (Regulation 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of regulations 5, 6, 7(1), 8, 9, 10, 11, 18 and 51 shall be formal requirements for purposes of section 29(1). Where section 29(2) applies, the Registrar shall notify the applicant of his findings and the applicant shall make any observation or amendment within three months from date of mailing of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines which regs are treated as formalities and provides three-month response period to Registrar's formalities findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination (Regulation 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for substantive examination must be made on Form 5 with payment of prescribed fee within 18 months from filing date (four years for international application entering national phase); where application is divided a further request is needed at time of filing divisional; request should, where appropriate, be accompanied by information on related earlier applications/patents and results of searches/examinations including certified English translations; Registrar may waive requirements under subregulation (3); Registrar shall inform applicant if application deemed withdrawn under section 29A(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict time limits (18 months generally; 4 years for national phase international apps); provide prior art/patent family info and search results to assist examination; Registrar has waiver discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for modified substantive examination (Regulation 27A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for modified substantive examination shall be made on Form 5A with prescribed fee within 18 months from filing date (4 years for international national phase); for divisional applications a further request must be made at time of filing division; request must be accompanied by certified true copy of granted patent(s) in prescribed countries and certified translations and proposed amendments to conform where descriptions/claims/drawings differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modified substantive examination is tied to corresponding foreign/granted patents and requires evidence and possibly amendments to bring documents into conformity; time limits mirror Reg 27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferment for filing request for examination and providing information (Regulation 27B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for deferment of filing a substantive or modified substantive examination request or for provision of required information/documents must be made on Form 5B; maximum deferment periods for filing a request or providing required information/documents are five years from filing date, subject to specific subregulation conditions; where applicant cannot file modified substantive exam request within five-year period they may file a substantive exam request within three months after expiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanism to defer examination-related filings up to five years; a fallback to substantive exam request exists if modified exam request deadline missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination substantive requirements and searches (Regulation 27C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of sections 13–16 Part V, sections 26, 26A, 26B, 27 and specified regulations shall be substantive requirements for section 30(1). Examiner shall search such documents as Registrar deems necessary to determine compliance particularly with sections 14 and 15; upon Examiner's report Registrar may request further search or investigations; applicant may be given two months to make observations or amendments when section 30(3) applies; observations/amendments referred to Examiner who reports determination to Registrar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which statutory provisions are substantive for examination purposes, search obligations, referral and response periods (typically two months for substantive examination responses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified substantive examination substantive requirements (Regulation 27D)
rubrics_metrics.description: For modified substantive examination the requirements of sections 13 and 14 Part V and other named sections/regulations are substantive; additionally the description, claims and drawings whether as filed or amended must be the same or substantially the same (apart from matters of form) as the description, claims and drawings of the invention granted a patent or other title in the prescribed country/treaty; Examiner shall search documents as Registrar deems necessary; upon report Registrar may request further search/investigation; applicant given two months to make observations or amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modified substantive examination ties local application to the content of a corresponding granted foreign patent and requires substantial identity (aside from form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination grounds and procedure (Regulation 27E)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who has requested substantive examination may request expedited examination once application is available for public inspection; request must be in Form 5H with statutory declaration stating grounds and prescribed fee; Registrar may grant expedited exam if reasonably satisfied it is in national/public interest, infringement proceedings exist/potential infringement, applicant has commercialised or will commercialise within two years, grant required to obtain monetary benefits from Government/institutions recognized by Registrar, invention relates to green technologies, or other reasonable grounds; Registrar notifies applicant in writing; if granted applicant must file Form 5I and pay fee within five working days; for substantive examination, if Examiner reports non-compliance with requirements, Registrar gives the applicant an adverse report and one opportunity to make observations/amendments within three weeks; failure to amend deems expedited request withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited examination has special grounds, strict timelines (five working days to file forms and three weeks to respond to adverse report) and can be withdrawn for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of refusal must state reasons (Regulation 28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is refused under listed Act sections, the Registrar shall notify the applicant in writing of that decision and shall state the reasons therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written refusal with reasons is mandatory; provides basis for appeals or further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of grant contents (Regulation 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate of grant shall contain the patent number, name and address of owner, name of inventor (except where opt-out), filing date and priority date if any, date of grant, title of invention and date the certificate is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate enumerates key bibliographic data of the granted patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of patent document (Regulation 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent shall contain number, owner name/address, inventor name/address (unless opt-out), agent name/address (if any), filing date, priority date and country, date of grant, title, IPC symbol, abstract, description, claims and all drawings, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full specification and bibliographic data must be included in the granted patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register form and content (Regulation 31)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Register shall be kept in such form and medium as Registrar may determine and shall contain the particulars specified in Regulation 30(a)–(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar determines format; Register includes patent bibliographic particulars and is the official record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for certified copies/extracts (Regulation 31A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for certified copies or extracts for purposes of sections 33, 33A(2), 34 and 83A shall be made on Form 5C with payment of prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form 5C and pay appropriate fee as per Schedule I; certified copies are formal requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Register (Regulation 31B)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request under section 33B to amend the Register shall be made on Form 5D with payment of prescribed fee; Registrar may require submission of information or documents including a written explanation by owner in support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to the Register may demand supporting evidence and explanation; fees apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Gazette reference to grant (Regulation 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to the grant published in the Gazette shall include the particulars specified in Regulation 30(a)–(j) and the most illustrative drawing if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gazette entry mirrors patent bibliographic data and best drawing to inform the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual fees (Regulation 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribed annual fee shall be paid to the Registrar who shall record payment in the Register; lapse of a patent for non-payment shall be recorded; annual fees paid are not refundable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely payment of annual fees is mandatory to avoid lapse; non-refundable even if overpaid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of lapsed patent (Regulation 33A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for reinstatement under section 35A(1) shall be made on Form 5E with payment of prescribed fee; Registrar may require submission of information/documents including written explanation; where Registrar not satisfied he shall notify the requester with reasons and give opportunity to be heard; requester may ask for hearing within one month; Registrar shall give decision after hearing; if satisfied Registrar notifies and requester must within one month pay all annual fees due and prescribed surcharge for reinstatement; upon receipt Registrar shall reinstate and record date of reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement procedure includes opportunity for hearing, evidence submission, payment of arrears and surcharge; strict one-month windows for hearings and fees after notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for persons who exploit lapsed patents (Regulation 33B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has exploited or taken definite steps to exploit a patent after it is notified as lapsed and before it is reinstated may request a licence to exploit; request made on Form 5F and must serve a copy on patent owner; Registrar may require appearances and may grant licence subject to terms/conditions he deems fit and owner deemed to have consented; Registrar shall inform requester and owner in writing of decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides limited protection and licensing mechanism for third parties who relied on patent lapse; formal process with notice to owner and Registrar's discretionary terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of applications between patent and utility innovation (Regulation 33C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to convert application for patent into application for certificate for utility innovation or vice versa shall be made on Form 5G with payment of prescribed fee; Registrar shall notify if satisfied; upon notification requester shall pay additional prescribed fee within one month (different amounts depending on direction of conversion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion requires formal request, Registrar satisfaction, and timely payment of corresponding fees within one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners and Board of Examiners duties (Regulation 45 and following)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrar may appoint examiners; Board of Examiners (for patent agent registration/examinations) shall prepare and publish syllabus, determine study material, prepare papers, register and admit candidates, determine time/date/place for exams, award certificates, advise Registrar on persons satisfying requirements; Board may award/withdraw/withhold/cancel results and bar persons from examinations; Board may appoint examiners to set/assess/mark papers and give instructions as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the administrative and disciplinary powers of the Board and examiners for patent agent qualification and examinations; fees and allowances for appointed examiners may be paid as directed by Minister.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment to correct clerical errors in application or patent (Regulations 46 and 46A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to correct a clerical error or obvious mistake in an application shall be made on Form 16 with prescribed fee; requests to correct or amend a patent or associated document for clerical errors or other reasons shall be made on Form 16A with prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified form and fees; Registrar processes clerical/obvious corrections or other amendments per statutory section 79/79A procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing notice and procedure (Regulation 47)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrar shall give person entitled to a hearing under section 81 not less than one month's notice of the date; within 21 days of the notice the person shall inform Registrar whether he desires to be heard; failure to inform within 21 days allows Registrar to proceed in absence; Registrar may invite an Examiner to assist in hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-month minimum notice and 21-day response requirement; failure to respond may result in hearing in absentia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures for partnerships, companies and associations (Regulation 50)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents signed on behalf of a partnership must contain full names of partners and be signed by all partners or by qualified partner stating he signs on behalf; corporate documents signed by director/secretary/principal officer or other person who satisfies Registrar of authority; associations' documents may be signed by any person appearing to Registrar to be duly qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar may require proof of authority; strict signature rules depending on entity type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address for service in Malaysia (Regulation 51)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person concerned with proceedings under the Act and every owner of a patent shall furnish to the Registrar an address for service in Malaysia on Form 20 with prescribed fee, which may be treated for all purposes as the person's address; where a patent agent is appointed the address for service shall be the address of the agent; Form 20 not required if address already furnished in another prescribed form and unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An in-Malaysia address for service is compulsory and often provided via agent; fees apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by post and time of receipt (Regulation 52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents required or authorized to be filed can be delivered by hand during business hours or sent by post; sending by post is deemed effected by properly addressing, preparing and posting a prepaid letter and deemed received when actually received at Patent Registration Office; filing is deemed effected when received and recorded as received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postal filing is allowed but receipt/time of filing is when Office receives and records the document; ensure proper postage and addressing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing of documents (Regulation 52A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrar may provide electronic filing service; a person intending to use the service must comply with terms and conditions specified by the Registrar (published on official website or by notice); an electronically filed document is deemed effected when accepted by the electronic filing system; accompanying documents not capable of electronic filing may be delivered by other permitted manners subject to Registrar-specified terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing acceptance time is system acceptance; users must follow Registrar terms and conditions and handle non-electronic companion documents per Registrar's directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and conditions for electronic filing and grounds for refusal (Regulation 52B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms and conditions for electronic filing include procedure to comply with, format/media for recording/storing, manner of authenticating documents including digital signatures, and actions on interruption; Registrar may refuse to accept/register any electronically filed document where information is not legible, electronic record not storable, record appears altered/damaged/incomplete/forged, or terms/conditions not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies technical and authentication standards for e-filing and enumerates clear grounds for Office refusal of electronic filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for extension of time (Regulation 53)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request under section 82 for extension of time shall be made to the Registrar on Form 21 with payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form 21 and pay fee as per Schedule I; extensions are formal requests subject to Registrar discretion and statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule I — detailed fee schedule and itemised matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule I lists itemised matters/proceedings and corresponding e-filing and manual fees and the form numbers; covers request for grant, claims fees per claim, entering national phase fees, reinstatement surcharges, examination fees, expedited examination, assignments, licences, copies, annual renewal fees per year, patent agent examination fees, appeals, extensions of time (monthly surcharges) and many other items with specified RM amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/agents must consult Schedule I for exact amounts and whether e-filing or manual rates apply; includes percentage surcharges for late payments and detailed annual fee progression by year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule II — prescribed forms (Schedule II note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule II lists the Forms referenced in the Regulations (forms are not reproduced in the document; note directs users to forms menu).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the prescribed form for each act; refer to the Office's forms menu or Registrar for the actual form content.
